practice.title: Sentiment Classifier via Transformers.js
practice.taskOpening: Build `classifyReports(reports, pipelineFactory)`. The first argument is an array of report strings. Return [] immediately for an empty list, without loading a pipeline. The second stands in for `pipeline()`: call it with the name of the task you want, await it once, and it resolves to a callable model for that task. There is no default task. It rejects a name the library does not ship, and a task that is not the one this job needs answers in a shape carrying neither a label nor a score. Return an array of `{ text, label, score }` ordered by score descending, most confident first, whatever the label. Load the pipeline once and pass the whole array to the classifier in one call: reloading per report is the anti-pattern the lesson warns about, and the tests count both calls. The classifier answers positionally, one prediction per report in the order you sent them, so join each report to its own prediction before you reorder anything.

practice.title: Detect Anomalies with Z-Score
practice.taskOpening: Write `isAnomaly(value, mean, std)` that returns true when the reading sits more than 3 standard deviations from the mean, in either direction. The baseline is not fixed: `mean` and `std` arrive as arguments and change from one call to the next, so the allowed distance has to be computed from them on every call. Both routes are graded the same, the tensor one (`tf.scalar`, then `.dataSync()[0]` to read the number back out) and plain arithmetic. Inputs must be finite and std must be nonnegative; reject invalid inputs. If std is zero, compare value with mean directly: equality is normal and any difference is flagged under this exercise's exact-reading policy. No z-score exists in that case. Real sensors need an explicitly chosen measurement tolerance.

practice.title: Temporal Attention Over a Window
practice.taskOpening:
Build `temporalAttention(sequence, scorerWeights)`. `sequence` is a [T, d] tensor of readings; `scorerWeights` is a [d + 1, 1] linear scorer whose last row weights position. Concatenate a position column onto the readings, evenly spaced from 0 at the first step to 1 at the last. Score every step with one matMul, then softmax those scores into `weights`, a [T] tensor holding one weight per step. Pool the ORIGINAL readings under those weights into a [d] `summary`, and return `{ summary, weights }` with both still tensors. Skip the position column and the scorer's shape will not line up.
Remove only the batch axis. A value width of one must still return shape [1], not a scalar. The sequence is non-empty; for a single time step its position is 0. Free intermediates with tf.tidy, preserving caller-owned inputs and both returned tensors.

practice.title: Inference Result Cache (Quantized Input Hash)
practice.taskOpening: Build a cache that hashes input tensors so near-identical inputs hit the same entry. `makeInferenceCache(model, decimals = 2, maxEntries = 100)` returns `{ predict(input), stats }`, and stats counts hits and misses. On a miss, predict runs the model and stores the result; on a hit it returns the stored result and does not run the model.

practice.title: Incident: Cache Served a Verdict From the Old Model
practice.taskOpening: PAGER: after this morning's model deploy, the dashboard showed a classification the new model disagrees with. It came from the cache. Build `auditCache(entries, currentVersion, now, ttlSeconds)`: an entry must be REFRESHED if its modelVersion differs from currentVersion (a deploy invalidates every cached verdict, no matter how fresh) OR its age (now - cachedAt, seconds) exceeds ttlSeconds. An age of exactly ttlSeconds has not exceeded it, so that entry is still served. Everything else passes this age/version policy, not a general correctness test. Assume valid timestamps no later than now and nonnegative finite TTL. The version identifies both weights and preprocessing; approximate-key collisions need separate checks. Return { serve, refresh } as arrays of keys, preserving input order.
